newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris ponders quota of women election candidates.
newsitem.headline: Paris ponders quota of women election candidates.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe is considering imposing quotas of women candidates on electoral lists, although most parliamentarians would vote against such a law, the daily Le Monde said on Friday.
It said Juppe's conservative government was studying whether to propose legislation introducing such quotas ahead of legislative elections in 1998.
France's opposition Socialists last month announced their candidates for next year's vote, 30 percent of whom are women.
A survey of French parliamentarians by Le Monde showed that 60 percent of those who answered were opposed to a quota system.
Of the National Assembly's 32 women members, 22 said they were against a quota.
The survey's participants -- 312 of the National Assembly's 576 members -- also largely opposed a constitutional amendment requiring an equal number of male and female candidates.
